newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sources detail extra 1996 jobless spending.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sources detail extra 1996 jobless spending.

text.p: The German government will be forced by the economic slowdown to increase its supplement to the Federal Labour Office by seven billion marks and its payments of unemployment assistance by 5.5 billion, government sources said on Friday.

Sources at the Federal Labour Office had said last week that the Office would need a supplement of around 12 billion marks this year, up from 4.3 billion originally budgeted, due to the worse than expected economic slowdown.

The Government sources said Friday that the supplement would amount to 11.3 billion marks. The Federal Labour Office runs the country's unemployment benefit system but Bonn is legally obliged to cover any shortfall in its budget.
The sources said that Federal spending on unemployment assistance would rise to 22.5 billion marks from the originally planned 17 billion marks.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel has already predicted a rise since reforms to assistance payments had been slowed by the opposition Social Democrats in the upper house of parliamentary and only came into effect on July 1.

Unemployment benefit is paid for a certain time by the Labour Office to those who become unemployed. After this time the Federal government pays unemployment assistance which is lower than unemployment benefit.
Unemployment assistance is paid to the unemployed via the Labour Office but is not part of the Office's budget.
The sources said the extra spending forced on the government made it all the more urgent to push through Bonn's austerity package which aims to slash spending by 70 billion marks in 1997.
